text: Git branching is a key skill for version control. Developers create feature branches to work on new ideas without affecting the main code. Each branch is like a separate copy where changes can be tested safely. When the work is ready, the team uses merging to bring changes back into the main project. Before merging, they often open pull requests so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This workflow keeps projects organised and reduces mistakes. By using branches, teams can work together at the same time and keep the main version stable and reliable.
